episodes.title: Gas reservation policy gets green light

stories.story: National domestic gas reservation scheme announcement
stories.angle: A necessary measure to put downward pressure on household and industry costs vs government facing a bumpy road through parliament
stories.voices: Jack Mackay, Political Reporter (live); Madeleine King, Minister for Resources (pre-recorded); David Shoebridge, Greens Senator (pre-recorded); Saul Kavnic, MST Financials Head of Energy Research (pre-recorded)
stories.tone: Explanatory and neutral, presenting competing stakeholder views
stories.emphasis: Consumer and industry cost pressures, policy details, and political friction
stories.evidence: 00:42 "Australian gas it becomes more affordable to Australians. That's really at the heart of this." — Madeleine King

stories.story: Victorian state election eve polling and political mood
stories.angle: Victoria heads to the polls with an election set to deliver a verdict on 12 years of Labor power
stories.voices: Samantha Maiden, Political Reporter (live); Glenn Waverley, voter (clip); Jackie Sun, voter (clip)
stories.emphasis: Voter sentiment, polling consistency, and the mood for change
stories.evidence: 03:21 "Polls have been consistently showing Victorians are in the mood for change" — Samantha Maiden

stories.story: Western Sydney data centre boom and local community impact
stories.angle: Rapid tech infrastructure expansion brings economic growth but triggers community concern over local planning and environmental impact
stories.voices: Nandiri Deer, Reporter (live); Navana Prasad, local resident (live); Christie Junche, grassroots campaigner (live)
stories.tone: Investigative and empathetic to local residents
stories.emphasis: Community pushback, scale of development, and planning consultation
stories.evidence: 06:36 "Navana Prasad has grown up watching her neighborhood on Sydney's outer western fringe evolve from farmland into an industrial hub." — Nandiri Deer

stories.story: Aged care and medical workforce parental leave discrimination
stories.angle: Systemic discrimination against pregnant women and mothers in the medical workforce
stories.voices: Samantha Dick, Reporter (live); Dr Benny Samadi, medical researcher (pre-recorded)
stories.emphasis: Pregnancy discrimination in medical training and employment
stories.evidence: 09:54 "first realised how hard it is to be a mother in medicine" — Dr Benny Samadi

stories.story: Retail sector Black Friday sales outlook
stories.angle: Retailers hope for a sales bounce amid cost-of-living pressures
stories.voices: Harvey Norman and JB Hi-Fi representatives (referred); North Brisbane Uni student (clip)
stories.emphasis: Cost of living impact on consumer spending
stories.evidence: 13:22 "just means to just go out and get some good deals honestly" — North Brisbane Uni student

episodes.title: Australia's cyber security coordinator says cyber hygiene never been more important

stories.story: Global and domestic cyber security threats and data breaches
stories.angle: Cyber attacks are wreaking havoc globally, making robust cyber hygiene critical for Australia
stories.voices: Sally Sara, Host (live); Penny Wong, Foreign Minister (clip)
stories.emphasis: Rising frequency of cyber attacks and government warnings
stories.evidence: 00:09 "Cyber attacks have been wreaking havoc across the globe in recent months" — Sally Sara

stories.story: Artificial intelligence data centres and cyber risks
stories.angle: Increased artificial intelligence data centre deployment on Australian soil increases cyber security vulnerability
stories.voices: Sally Sara, Host (live); Michelle McGuinness, National Cyber Security Coordinator (live)
stories.emphasis: Risk management, technological sophistication of threats, and regulatory capability
stories.evidence: 01:22 "I actually think it increases our ability to understand and to shape the technology" — Michelle McGuinness

episodes.title: Resources Minister: government won't set target price for gas under reservation scheme

stories.story: Domestic gas reservation scheme and pricing policy
stories.angle: Government defends gas reservation policy while refusing to set target prices
stories.voices: Sally Sara, Host (live); Madeleine King, Minister for Resources (live); Susan McDonald, Shadow Minister for Resources (clip)
stories.emphasis: Gas pricing mechanisms, export impacts, and industry consultation
stories.evidence: 00:27 "what do you consider to be affordable for consumers? What's the benchmark?" — Sally Sara

episodes.title: Coalition concerned gas reservation policy will discourage investment in new gas projects

stories.story: Coalition criticism of the domestic gas reservation scheme
stories.angle: Opposition warns the reservation policy will discourage investment in new gas projects and damage energy supply
stories.voices: Sally Sara, Host (live); Bridget McKenzie, Shadow Minister for Infrastructure (live); Madeleine King, Minister for Resources (clip)
stories.emphasis: Investment certainty, gas supply risks, and economic impacts
stories.evidence: 00:25 "we've been able to secure a lot of important concessions, Sally" — Bridget McKenzie

episodes.title: Israeli Opposition Leader Gadi Eisenkot says he hopes to form a government within a week

stories.angle: Israeli opposition figures express optimism about forming a new government amid ongoing political deadlock
stories.voices: Sally Sara, Host (live); Gadi Eisenkot, Israeli Opposition politician (pre-recorded); Lahav Harkov, Jewish Insider Senior Political Correspondent (live)
stories.emphasis: Coalition prospects, political timelines, and regional stability
stories.evidence: 00:55 "At this point there are two preliminary political deals between Gadi Eisenkot's party and other parties" — Lahav Harkov

episodes.title: Spanish voters prepare to go to polls, as popularity of PM Pedro Sanchez plummets

stories.story: Spanish general election and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's popularity
stories.angle: Spain faces a pivotal general election driven by cost-of-living pressures and declining support for Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez
stories.voices: Sally Sara, Host (live); Jose Oliveras, Associate Professor, National Distance Education University (live)
stories.emphasis: Economic hardship, political polarization, and voter sentiment
stories.evidence: 00:55 "we may see a big change in government" — Jose Oliveras

episodes.title: Victoria heads to the polls

stories.story: Victorian state election preview and final campaign state of play
stories.angle: Victoria heads to the voting booths with Labor's 12-year incumbency facing strong electoral tests
stories.voices: Sally Sara, Host (live); Richard Willingham, State Political Reporter (live); Tony Barry, Redbridge Group Director (live)
stories.emphasis: Polling dynamics, marginal seats, and voter attitudes toward leadership
stories.evidence: 00:50 "the polls have the coalition's primary more than 10 points ahead of Labor's" — Richard Willingham

episodes.title: Victoria: It's Time?

stories.story: Victorian state election final countdown and political landscape
stories.angle: A comprehensive look at whether Victoria is ready for a change of government after 12 years of Labor rule

stories.emphasis: Policy differences, leadership impressions, and electoral volatility
